Scatter3d projection objects

Source: R/zz-gen-scatter3d.R
go_scatter3d_projection.Rd

The object for the projection of a scatter3d trace (go_scatter3d()). go_scatter3d_projection() creates one, with exactly its properties; a named list with the same properties works too.

Usage

go_scatter3d_projection(
  arg = NULL,
  ...,
  x = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  z = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

arg

Optional named list, or graph object of the same type, to initialise properties from. Named arguments take precedence.

...

Not used: properties must be named in full.

x

A go_scatter3d_projection_axis() object or named list, with properties opacity, scale and show (see go_scatter3d_projection_axis()).

y

A go_scatter3d_projection_axis() object or named list, with properties opacity, scale and show (see go_scatter3d_projection_axis()).

z

A go_scatter3d_projection_axis() object or named list, with properties opacity, scale and show (see go_scatter3d_projection_axis()).

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

Value

A go_scatter3d_projection object (a named list).

Details

Nested objects are named lists, or objects of the constructors their arguments name. Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when the object is created or modified. A property may be a one-sided formula (color = ~col): it is kept, and evaluated in the data (then checked) when its trace is added to a figure with add_<trace>() or add_trace().

Examples

mtcars |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter3d(
    x = ~wt,
    y = ~hp,
    z = ~mpg,
    projection = go_scatter3d_projection()
  )
